implemented: Shared validation/normalization for Pi, Codex and Claude model/thinking/startup_args/env before protocol compilation or Herdr mutation.
Claude protocol launch passes thinking through --effort; original terminal launch uses the same mapping.
Codex thinking merges into turn_options rather than discarding other fields; conflicting model/effort declarations are rejected.
Canonical legacy model/thinking prefixes are removed once before command reconstruction. Remaining duplicate shortcut switches are rejected.
Malformed option tables, non-string/NUL startup arguments, malformed environment values and unsupported thinking levels are rejected before launch.

verification.red: The first new Pi model/thinking case failed before implementation because whitespace/case were not normalized.
coverage: Every thinking level in the existing Python contract
Herdr dry-run rejection before runtime files
Existing config formats and native startup lifetimes
Claude Herdr model/effort forwarding and stable reconnect

remaining_permission_gap.finding: Rust config compilation copies top-level permission but native runtime has no permission/permission_default/auto_permission consumer. Python launchers apply auto and role command policy explicitly.
remaining_permission_gap.required_next_work: Migrate explicit provider permission policy with role restrictions and caller authorization; validate both protocol and terminal paths before production/default promotion.

limits: Supported thinking presets follow the existing repository contract; model-specific availability remains the provider authority.
This is not complete ccb.config/API/provider flag parity. Arbitrary terminal-only startup flags, role command enforcement, permission mode and broader legacy migration remain pending.
No real Herdr UI or production installation changes in this patch.
